messages.subject: Re: How to use rbase in the RHIPE?
messages.subject_clean: How to use rbase in the RHIPE?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Well rbase was just an experimental package. hardly tested and certainly robust. I wont be providing much support to this - you'll probably need to read the sources.
have you installed it? have you read the function help?

This creates a table
    library(rJava)
    library(rbase)
    hb <- rb.init()
    crashers <- rb.table.new <http://rb.table.new>(hb,"crash.signatures",model, meta, additional)

A table called crash.signatures with 3 column families: model, meta, additional
      crasher <- rb.table.connect(hb,"crash.signatures")
      rhsz <- function (x) .Call("rh_sz",x); rhuz <- function(x) .Call("rh_uz",x)

This connects to the table (the other two lines are required because of a bug)

      crasher$putOne(k[[1]], values=list("model:data"=r,'meta:dummy'=TRUE)) ## because of bug, need at least two names

Here, i put one key-value pair into the database with k[[1]] as the key. model:data is a column-family-column label combination

And here is how i can retrieve documents

  crasher <- rb.table.connect(hb,"crash.signatures")
  getSig <- function(x,handle=crasher){
    lapply( handle$get(x,what='model:data'),function(r) rhuz(r$"model:data"))
  }
  getSig(P[1:2])

Hope it helps. I dont care much for Hbase ...

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Too many files open Error
messages.body_plain:
Yes, Fishtank,.

This is on EC2. I am running a job which is basically calculating I/O timings. And time taken to perform a function per core. This repeats across datasets. And each dataset (or correctly said as subset) is replicated thrice. This happened which the function was being applied to one of the replicates in the second subset. I am not sure if it overran the ram. I did have 69 Gigs of Ram per node and I had 1+3 Nodes. The name node was working as a data node and as a slave as well. Might it have something to do with that? Probably isolate the job of a name node?

Unfortunately, although I know about this problem its difficult to put a finger on the code or on the system and its resources.

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Too many files open Error
messages.body_plain:
Hey Fishtank,

I am not sure if just increasing the number of open files might be the solution. Could there be a situation that the number of open files exceed the increased capacity as well? So was thinking about the core of the problem. I think I might have got a direction here. If you would be kind enough to take a look at this link -> http://mail-archives.apache.org/mod_mbox/hadoop-hdfs-user/201208.mbox/%3C502271D...@cs.uni-kassel.de%3E <http://mail-archives.apache.org/mod_mbox/hadoop-hdfs-user/201208.mbox/%3C...@cs.uni-kassel.de%3E> . The response for which is -> http://mail-archives.apache.org/mod_mbox/hadoop-hdfs-user/201208.mbox/%3C6D57A8EB-E13B-4A1...@gmail.com%3E <http://mail-archives.apache.org/mod_mbox/hadoop-hdfs-user/201208.mbox/%3C...@gmail.com%3E> . Not sure if it is the right response. But do you think it might be a problem with too many open log files? If so then probably Hadoop is not cleaning up properly after its job?

IF you actually look at the code -> http://grepcode.com/file/repo1.maven.org/maven2/com.ning/metrics.serialization-all/2.1.0/org/apache/hadoop/mapred/TaskRunner.java which is for task runner, from line 279 to line 295. It is actually preparing new log files and directories for the same.
It looks like the directory is being made but not the log file. The boolean flag is not negated in the error message, so thats my guess.
